summary: Return the length of the longest contiguous strictly increasing or strictly decreasing run.
mainInsight: Scan once keeping the length of the current increasing run and of the current decreasing run: extend one and reset the other (equal neighbours reset both). Track the maximum seen.
canonicalApproach: Single pass with run starts or lengths

approaches.name: Single pass with run starts or lengths

cards.answer: Single pass tracking the current increasing run and the current decreasing run. Clue: It asks for the longest contiguous stretch that is monotone, and each next element either extends the stretch or breaks it, so counters in one pass are enough.
keyPoints: It asks for the longest contiguous stretch that is monotone, and each next element either extends the stretch or breaks it, so counters in one pass are enough.
cards.explanation: A contiguous run only depends on the previous neighbour, so keeping two run lengths and the maximum covers everything.

cards.answer: Single pass: extend the matching run, reset the other
cards.explanation: A comparison with the previous element either extends or breaks each run.

cards.answer: Equal elements are neither strictly increasing nor decreasing, so any run through the equal pair is broken: both the increasing and decreasing runs restart at the current element.
cards.explanation: A run of length 1 is always valid.
Equal elements break every run, so the best is 1. In the second array the decreasing run [9,7,4,1] has length 4 (the increasing run [2,6,9] has 3).

incorrectOptionExplanations.3, and 4: Equal neighbours are neither strictly increasing nor decreasing.
incorrectOptionExplanations.1, and 3: The decreasing run [9,7,4,1] is longer than the increasing run [2,6,9].
incorrectOptionExplanations.3, and 6: The array first increases, then decreases; no single run covers all six.
